full_judgment:
2. Facts leading to this appeal may be briefly noticed to begin with. The appellant by Memo No. 445/1/3(6)/JM dated 8-12-94 made a long report running into few pages to the Secretary. Cabinet Division in connection with the order of his conviction in Misc. (violation) Case No. 31 of 1994 and sentenced to 3 months civil imprisonment and fine of Taka 5,000.00 passed by the Assistant Judge of Ulipur. It is on record that an appeal, Misc. Appeal No. 76 of 1994, against the said order of conviction and sentence was pending at that time. 

 4. In his rambling report (he is found to have sent similar reports before) he referred to various other cases and observed that the local Judicial Officers including the District Judge were in a conspiracy against him as they became inimical towards him for his official acts done in the due discharge of duty and further that they were tarnishing the image of the administration for personal reasons. In making his observations he imputed improper motives to the Judicial Officers and made discourteous comments about them. 

 So, the reporting by the contemner about the local Judicial Officers to the different agencies of the Government are ex facie illegal and for which he must pay. The reportings by the contemner to the authorities against the local judicial officers are considered to malign the latter (Judicial Officers) which comes under the mischief of contempt of Court and this kind of unwarranted activities of the contemner should not be allowed to go unpunished, otherwise there will be anarchy and hooliganism between the different branches of the administration and thereby the image of the Government will be at stake. 

 10. Khandkar Mahbubuddin Ahmed, learned Advocate appearing for the appellant, submitted that he would not utter one word in defence of the appellant except saying that the appellant was ill advised himself from the beginning in making the impugned report in particular against the Judicial Officers specially when his appeal against his own conviction was pending and he was not also well advised when he was called upon to show cause for his discourteous and objectionable remarks made against the Judicial Officers of Kurigram. Mr. Ahmed submitted that the remarks were without doubt objectionable and certainly not expected of a high and responsible official as the appellant was. It was, of course, part of his official duty to report to higher authority for guidance about the difficulties and problems he might have been facing in running the local administration because of proceedings in Court but that would never justify using indecorous language and making comments against Judicial Officers imputing motives to their judgments and orders. Mr. Ahmed submitted that the appellant should have tendered unqualified apology before the High Court Division at the first opportunity without trying to explain the facts of the various cases which formed the subject matter of his report. Unfortunately, he did not get proper advice at that time. 

 1. The appellant filed an application tendering unconditional apology and praying for exonerating him from conviction in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 1356 of 1997. But, unfortunately, the same has not been properly drawn up and, as such, the appellant sought leave of this High Court to file a supplementary affidavit to correct the same for the kind consideration of this High Court.
